item.text: I’m reading the current sorter again and looking for the next real simplification instead of just renaming methods. The remaining friction is in the way `MaxHeap` still computes structural relationships itself, so I’m targeting the index arithmetic next.

I found a better consolidation point than another tiny helper: the heap boundary object and the index-arithmetic helpers belong together. I’m merging those concerns into a single heap-shape helper so `MaxHeap` stops knowing about both range math and tree math.
The shape/range merge is in place. I’m compiling and running the demo again to make sure moving the heap-structure logic behind `HeapWindow` didn’t change the result.

Refactored [HeapSort.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/036_heap_sort/HeapSort.java:1) again by merging the heap-boundary state and the tree-shape math into a single `HeapWindow` helper. `MaxHeap` no longer computes child indexes or root handling directly; it delegates those structural details to `HeapWindow`.

That reduces the number of concepts `MaxHeap` owns at once and makes it more narrowly responsible for the sift/swap behavior. Verification: `javac HeapSort.java HeapSortDemo.java` succeeded, and `java -cp . HeapSortDemo` still outputs `[2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10]`.
